title: Where does an archetype's example content come from, and which settings must an author supply?
description: ST-DECL-UC01-R01 and R04 say each archetype supplies the smallest example content that checking accepts, and R05 says an empty scaffold names every setting the author must supply. Today the scaffolds of rpc-service and browser-service are refused: rpc-service needs the grpc-processes settings processes and proto_files, a proto file and a process factory package (factory/rpc.go) that imports the generated packages by the module path; browser-service needs a distinct api_prefix. The Archetype entity (ST-SUP-EN03) has no field that holds example content, and a component schema marks as required both settings the declaration must give and settings that only the running service gets (such as connection_string of postgres-adapter and issuer of jwt-auth), so checking cannot tell which settings an author must supply. Options: (a) add to the Archetype an example content field (files under the archetype folder and the settings to write into the declaration, with the module path as a placeholder), and mark in a component schema each setting the declaration must give, so that checking refuses its absence and init can name it; (b) keep the example content in Declaring's code, one case per archetype; (c) narrow R01, R04 and R05 to archetypes that can be empty, such as rest-crud. Recommendation: (a), since the UC01 notes say the archetype supplies its example content, and a registry change then needs no change to STEGO's code. Until then UC01-R01, R04-T01, R05 and the flow test stay not automated; rest-crud, which can be empty, already passes as written.

title: Must stego validate --json report the tenancy, audit and mode defaults for a service on the GORM store, which does not use them?
description: The CLI tour (2026-11-10, scene A27) ran stego validate --json on a rest-crud service whose record states the data path store. The settings it reports hold pooled tenancy with the key and claim tenant_id, audit at level change with a SHA-256 chain, an anchor, the sink audit-sink and pii redact, the entity tenant owned and the modes api, worker and controller, each marked as a default. Only the runtime data path (ST-SUP-RC01-OC41) carries out these settings; the store path does not, so the report tells the author of a store service that it has tenancy, audit and modes that it does not have. The records ask for the report as it is: ST-DECL-INV18 and ST-DECL-UC05-R01 say that every declaration that omits tenancy or audit gets pooled tenancy and audit at level change, ST-DECL-UC09-R01 says that one that omits modes gets all, and ST-DECL-UC05-R01-T01 runs on ST-DECL-TD02, which is on the store, and expects these defaults. Options: (a) report these settings only for a service on the runtime data path; for a store service leave them out of settings, and change INV18, UC05-R01, UC09-R01 and the tests to say so, with a test data set on the runtime path for UC05-R01-T01; (b) keep the report, and add to the document a member data_path (runtime or store) and, for a store service, a note on each setting that the store does not carry out; (c) keep the report as it is, because the settings describe the declaration and not the data path. Recommendation: (b), because the declaration stays the same on both paths, the settings stay true of the declaration, and the author and an agent then see both what the declaration gets and that the store does not carry it out, with no change of the design records that a move to the runtime path will need again.

title: Which step of Record what a service was built from fulfills that apply writes the record inside the service's repo?
description: ST-GEN-UC01-R05 says that apply MUST write the record inside the service's repo, beside the code it generated. Only the step ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S02 (the service author commits the record with the generated code) fulfills it, and that step invokes no command, so no technical record can build the requirement, although ST-GEN-UC01-R05-T01 is automated and passes. Options: (a) ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S01, which invokes Apply a plan (ST-GEN-CMD01), also fulfills ST-GEN-UC01-R05, and S02 keeps it too; (b) S02 also invokes Apply a plan; (c) the requirement stays proved and not built. Recommendation: (a), since apply is what writes the record in the repo and the commit only shows it.

title: Must a recorded input hold only the executable bit of the file mode, as version control keeps it?
description: The field Mode of Recorded input (ST-GEN-EN04) holds the file's permission bits, and Drift (ST-GEN-TM03) is any difference between a recorded input and the file on disk. The code records the full permission bits (for example 420, which is 0644) in the input manifest, puts them in its digest, and drift compares them. Git keeps only the executable bit. So a fresh clone of an example under the umask 002 gives service.yaml and .stego/config.yaml the mode 664 (436), stego drift reports two changed inputs and stego plan wants to update the compiler state, although nothing changed (CLI tour, 2026-11-10, scenes B05 and B06). Options: (a) Mode holds the mode as version control keeps it: 493 (0755) when the owner execute bit is set, else 420 (0644); STEGO records that value and drift and plan compare only it. The manifest format and its digest stay the same, every committed record that holds 420 stays valid with no regeneration, and a record that an apply wrote under another umask shows drift once, until the next apply. (b) Keep the full permission bits, and tell authors to clone and apply under the umask 022. (c) Remove Mode from the record, with a new manifest format version that changes every digest and needs a regeneration of each example. Recommendation: (a), because the record must not depend on what version control does not keep, and (a) changes no committed record.

title: What must the completion log of a failed command hold?
description: ST-SUP-RC32-OC09-T01 expects the completion log of ST-SUP-RP03-LC12 to hold only the code internal, and then the code reservation.short_stock. The completion log of the telemetry runtime holds the span fields only, the method, the route and the status, and no error code or text (ST-SUP-RP03-LC06), so it can hold no code. Options: (A) change the Then to expect that the completion log holds neither the email nor the SQL text, which its fields give; (B) add the fixed error code to the completion log in the telemetry runtime. Recommendation: A, because the status already tells the outcome and a smaller log leaks less. The test proves the response and the audit row now.

title: How many audit rows does a committed command leave?
description: ST-SUP-RC32-OC07 says the handler writes one audit row per command, and ST-SUP-RC32-OC07-T01 expects one command audit row with the outcome ok for a committed command. The command runtime writes one row for each write of the fill, with the command name as the action (ST-SUP-RP10-LC06), and no row for the command itself, so reserve-and-charge leaves two ok rows, one for its Reservation and one for its Charge. Options: (A) change ST-SUP-RC32-OC07 and its test to one ok row per write, with the command as the action; (B) add one ok row for the command itself to the runtime. Recommendation: A, because each row then holds the before and after of one resource. The test proves the rows of the writes now.

title: What does a command declare of its effect destinations and effect names?
description: The generated CommandSpec gives each effect destination of a command to the runtime as command.Destination with MustLand and Idempotent, but ST-DECL-EN18 declares only the destination and the effect name, and the destinations setting of a component gives only a name, so the generator sets MustLand and Idempotent to true for every destination. The runtime's CommandSpec also takes no effect names, so a fill can stage an effect name that the command does not declare; the generator refuses only a missing, malformed or repeated effect name in the declaration. Options: (A) the destinations setting declares must_land and idempotent for each destination, the generator reads them, and CommandSpec takes the declared effect names, which Stage then holds the fill to; (B) keep must land and idempotent for every command destination, and add only the effect names to CommandSpec; (C) keep both as they are. Recommendation: A, because the outbox worker registers each destination with these two properties and a staged effect should be one that the declaration names.

title: Which parent does a row go under when it refers to more than one entity with a resource type, or to one optionally?
description: ST-SUP-RP10-LC05 makes a create, and a move of a row with a Parent, decide the command's permission on the one parent that the row names, and the runtime's EntitySpec.Parent gives one parent. The command generator therefore refuses an entity with two or more references to entities with a resource type, such as an Order with customer_id to Customer and product_id to Product, and an entity whose one such reference is optional, such as a tree whose optional parent_id refers to its own entity, so that no parent goes undecided. The declaration cannot say which reference is the parent. Options: (A) ST-DECL-EN02 gets a parent field that names the one reference that is the parent, and the other references are decided as reads of their own resources, or not at all; an optional parent is decided when it is set, and a root row is decided on the command's resource; (B) Parent gives every such reference, and the runtime decides on each one; (C) keep the refusal. Recommendation: A, because a row has one place in the authorization tree and the declaration then says it; until then the refusal stays.

title: How does query.Serve answer a declared refusal with its status and code?
description: ST-SUP-RC33-OC07 says that the handler answers a declared refusal with its declared status and code, and any other error with 500 and the code internal, in the response, the audit row's error_code and the completion log. query.Serve (ST-SUP-RP11-LC17) answers every error it does not know with 500, and its problem response holds no code member; generated code cannot change the answer, because Serve writes it. The generator emits the typed refusal values and queries.Declared. Until this is decided a fill whose row went away after the decision before the fill returns queries.ErrNotFound, which Serve answers 404; a declared refusal such as order_unknown is answered 500. Options: (a) the runtime adds to query.HTTP a function such as Refusal func(error) (status int, code string, ok bool), which the generated code sets to queries.Declared, and Serve writes the code in the problem response and gives it to the read audit row and the completion log; (b) the runtime defines its own refusal type that generated code makes. Recommendation: (a). OC07 stays not built until this is decided.

title: Over which transport is a stream query served, and how does the generator know a query is a stream?
description: The query runtime has RunStream (ST-SUP-RP11-LC13) but no HTTP helper for a stream, and the declaration marks a query as a stream only by a gRPC method that is a server stream (ST-DECL-INV73), whose check is not built, so the compiler cannot tell the generator. The generator emits, for each query in gen.Context.QueryStreams, the stream slot type, a Bind function and a Stream function on query.RunStream for the transport; the service test carries the messages as JSON lines over HTTP itself. Options: (a) a stream is served over gRPC only: the compiler fills QueryStreams from the proto files when ST-DECL-INV73 is built, and the grpc-application component calls the generated Stream function; (b) the declaration gets a stream kind for HTTP and the runtime adds query.ServeStream (for example JSON lines), so the generated code passes only what varies; (c) both. Recommendation: (a), as the declaration states now; (b) only when an HTTP client needs a stream.

title: May a query fill import out/queries, the query slot's contract package?
description: ST-EXT-INV05 says that a fill imports only the package out/slots, which holds the contract of each slot. The query slot is a Go contract, not a protobuf message: its request, handle and fill types, repositories and refusals are in the generated package out/queries, which a query fill imports, and that package reaches the runtime library. ST-EXT-UC01-R03 says the slot's contract. Options: (a) INV05 names each slot's contract package: out/slots for a protobuf slot, out/queries for the query slot and the command generator's package for the command slot, and the import rule admits the packages of the runtime library that the contract reaches; (b) the capability generators emit their contracts into out/slots. Recommendation: (a), because the contract of the query slot needs the runtime library's types and out/slots is the compiler's. Until this is decided, stego test refuses evidence for a query fill (checkImports).

title: Is an update, a patch or a delete of a missing row answered 403 or 404 on the runtime data path?
description: On the store path a write to a row that is not there answers 404. On the runtime data path the write is a generated command (ST-SUP-RC20-OC37), and command.Run decides the command's permission before the fill with the same consistency whether or not the row exists, and answers a missing row as a deny, with ErrDenied (ST-SUP-RP10-LC31); ST-SUP-RC29-OC02-T03 expects 403 for a deny of an update. The generated handler therefore answers 403 for both; a row that the decision allows and the fill then does not find, such as a deleted row whose tuple stays, is 403 too, and 404 is only for an operation that decides no permission. Options: (A) keep 403 for a missing and a denied row, so the answer does not tell that a row exists; (B) answer 404 for both, as a read does (ST-SUP-RP11-LC06), and change ST-SUP-RC29-OC02-T03. Recommendation: A, because it is the runtime's rule for every command and the record of a deny already says 403.

title: What does a handler answer when an after slot fails after its command committed?
description: ST-SUP-RC20-OC34 says an after slot runs only after the command committed, and no slot contract says what the answer is when the after slot then fails. On the store path the handler answers 500 with the slot's error text, although the write is stored. On the runtime data path the write and its idempotency key row are committed with the response before the after slot runs, so a 500 would differ from the replay of the same key and would leak the slot's text. The generated handler on the runtime data path logs the failure with the slot name and no error text, counts it, and answers the committed response. Options: (A) answer the committed response and log the failure, as now; (B) answer a fixed 500 with no detail; (C) run the after slots through the outbox, so a failure is retried and never reaches the answer. Recommendation: A now and C later, because the client's write succeeded and a retry with its key gets the same answer.

title: Is the record at the base ref the project's record, or the committed one, until the check against a base ref is built?
description: ST-SUP-RC01-OC41 says that the compiler switches the runtime data path on only for a service whose base ref has no record. The orchestrator decided in the review of PR #187, under the Product owner's delegation, that the record states the data path of each run (data_path runtime or store, record format version 4), and that the compiler reads it from the project's record or, when the project has none checked out, from the record that the HEAD commit holds; a run of a service with the command and query generators that cannot read that commit, because git fails or the project is not in a repository, is refused, and the ledger never takes over a ledger row of a GORM release. A service with no record starts on the runtime data path when it has the command and the query generators; a record before format version 4 is of the store; a record on the store keeps the store until a declaration version bump (ST-GEN-UC10); a record on the runtime data path stays on it, and a run without one of the generators is refused with a fault that names this question; and the migration job refuses a database with tables that its ledger does not record, so a service whose record is lost cannot migrate over the GORM tables. Plan and apply have no base ref yet (ST-GEN-UC14). Options: (a) keep this reading until ST-GEN-UC14 gives plan the record at the base ref, then read data_path from that record; (b) read the record at the repository's default branch now. Recommendation: (a), because the change gate then names the base ref with the other checks of ST-GEN-UC14, and the committed record already covers a record that is not checked out.

title: Which prefix replaces stego.dev in the Kubernetes labels and annotations, and in the example predicate type, now that stego.dev belongs to another company?
description: The owner decided on 2026-11-10 that the runtime module path is github.com/jsell-rh/stego/registry/runtime, because stego.dev belongs to an unrelated company. That decision names the module path only. Other text still uses stego.dev as a name STEGO owns: the Kubernetes label and annotation keys that the generated services and the namespace allocation write (stego.dev/config-sha256 in ST-SUP-RC15-OC17 and ST-SUP-RC16-OC08; stego.dev/allocator, stego.dev/allocation-profile, stego.dev/network-spec-sha256, stego.dev/allocation-network-endpoints, stego.dev/pinned-namespace-uid and stego.dev/service-account-<alias> in the code of the kubernetes-service and kubernetes-client components and their scripts), the reserved owner-label prefix stego.dev of the kubernetes-service renderer, and the example of the predicate type field of ST-VO56 (https://stego.dev/attestations/proof-run/v1, while the code writes https://github.com/jsell-rh/stego/assure/proof-run/v1). A label key is a contract with a running cluster: a new prefix changes the selectors and the admission policies of every installed service, so it needs a migration. Options: (a) keep stego.dev for the label and annotation keys, because a Kubernetes prefix is a name and not a fetch, and change only the ST-VO56 example to the predicate type that the code writes; (b) move the keys to a prefix STEGO controls, such as stego.jsell-rh.github.io, with a migration that writes the new keys and reads both until every installed service has them; (c) as (b), with no migration, because no service is installed yet. Recommendation: (c) if no allocation is installed in a cluster, else (b); in both, change the ST-VO56 example now.
